title: Diagnosing oral and maxillofacial diseases using deep learning
summary: DOLNet, a multi-scale hierarchical-attention network, classifies and localizes odontogenic lesions on panoramic radiographs. The paper reports recall and F1 gains of up to 42.4% and 44.2% over recent methods, and 10.7% and 10.8% higher recall and F1 than clinicians. The authors note limited dataset access and generalization.

evidence.tested: DOLNet was evaluated on panoramic radiographs for odontogenic-lesion classification and localization and compared with recent methods and human clinicians. The paper reports recall and F1 gains of up to 42.4% and 44.2% over recent methods, and 10.7% and 10.8% higher recall and F1 than clinicians.
evidence.unknown: The authors identify limited access to large, well-annotated datasets; performance beyond the evaluated images and clinical settings is not established.
evidence.ai_role: DOLNet uses mutually influencing hierarchical attention across image scales to classify and localize odontogenic lesions in panoramic radiographs; the paper compares performance with clinicians and other methods.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
